answer: Each identity claims one grove plot and locks an 80-credit bond. Its hay load crosses the bridge scale, which logs gross and tare weight and area on a sealed ticket in the ledger. An auditor recomputes yield from the mesa table and checks the claim against the grove zenith cap; overclaim, a reused ticket, or a seal mismatch burns the bond. The k-th fee is 26+8(k-1); the 1000th costs 8018, so 1000 fakes pay 4022000 plus 80000 locked. A rented-load ring fails: one load cannot carry two plot seals. An honest identity pays 26 once and recovers its bond after audit.
